name: Maximum Degree
definition: The **maximum degree** of a concept class is defined as the maximum degree of its $1$-inclusion graph.
graph_summary: The largest vertex degree in the one-inclusion graph.
comments: Conditioning gives an induced subgraph of the $1$-inclusion graph, whose maximum degree cannot exceed that of the original graph.

monotonic.proof: The 1-inclusion graph of a subfamily is an induced subgraph of the original graph, so no vertex degree can increase.

c_monotonic.proof: Conditioning gives an induced subgraph of the one-inclusion graph, so maximum degree cannot increase.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{000,001,110\}$ has one-inclusion graph consisting of one edge and an isolated vertex, hence maximum degree 1. Projecting to the last two coordinates gives $\{00,01,10\}$, the three-vertex path of maximum degree 2.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
